max: Quick share — ran an nsys trace against the dedicated pool after the RC that caused the ~3% p99 latency regression. Short findings below, attaching timeline link: https://perf.internal/nsys/trace/abc123 :eyes:

olivia: Nice, can you paste the kernel list and the batching stats?

max: sure. nvprof shows a subset where some GEMM kernels fell back to fp32 path (kernel name: gemm_fp32_fallback). Also saw skewed queue time vs compute time when continuous-batching window grew. Snippet:```
Kernel: gemm_fp32_fallback    Calls: 124    TotalTime(ms): 87.4    Avg(ms): 0.705
Kernel: gemm_q8_fast          Calls: 412    TotalTime(ms): 102.1   Avg(ms): 0.248
Kernel: softmax_f32           Calls: 520    TotalTime(ms): 23.8    Avg(ms): 0.045
```

max: KV cache numbers: hit-rate dropped from 91% -> 79% for the 8k key-id namespace after the checkpoint rotation. That maps to extra decode steps and more KV reads per token. KV lookup breakdown in perfetto: ```
kv_lookup_ms: 0.6 -> 1.1 (avg)
kv_miss_extra_decode: +0.18ms/token on tail requests
```

dario: Did the kernel fallback coincide with any change in compile flags or quantization plugin?

max: Yep — the kernel selector fell back because a small subset of layers had dynamic shapes from the new tokenizer change. The selector couldn't match the fast q8 kernel signature so it used fp32 path. I captured the selector decision table in the trace (column: selector_reason).

sophie: Can you share timeline highlights? queue vs compute ratios?

max: From perf timeline (nsys): average queue_time per batch jumped from 12ms -> 37ms for high-concurrency bursts. Compute_time per batch stayed ~18ms. So overall tail increased because queue time now dominates. Continuous-batching window widened ~+25ms which allowed more aggregation but increased tail for latency-sensitive single-request flows. Visual: https://perf.internal/perfetto/timeline/xyz789

max: Quick root-cause hypothesis: tokenizer change -> occasional shape variance -> kernel selector mismatch -> use slower fp32 kernels + KV cache churn from checkpoint rotation -> increased per-request KV misses -> longer queue times due to head-of-line blocking in the batching queue.

olivia: Nice write-up. Any quick mitigations?

max: Short-term: force selector override to prefer q8 kernels for those layer shapes (runtime flag), roll back tokenizer patch for a canary, and ensure checkpoint rotation updates key-id maps synchronously (avoid in-place atomics). Medium: add selector fuzz tests and add trace-based alerts for selector falling back > 1% of calls.

perf-bot: @channel Canary rollout 2024-06-18 03:22 -> selector-override flag deployed to dedicated-canary. Monitor p95/p99.

dario: For follow-up, let's add a perfetto marker at the batching queue entry/exit to get precise per-request queuing histograms. Also add a kv cache metric: key-id stale counters.

max: Agreed. I'll attach the nsys capture and a small script to parse selector decisions and bucket queue_time by model and request-size. Will push to the perf repo.

sophie: thx — ping once the canary numbers roll in, will re-run evals against our latency-sensitive prompts. :thumbsup:

max: will do.
